Smoked spatchcock turkey + extra breasts

Ingredients & instructions
  • 20–22 lb whole turkey, spatchcocked
  • 9–11 lb additional turkey breasts
  • 2 packages Meat Church Bird Baptism brine (2025 baseline)
  • Meat Church Hickory and Hail Mary rubs (probable)
  • Compound butter (see separate recipe)
  • Turkey injection (see separate recipe)
  1. Prepare and fully chill brine according to package directions; use food-safe refrigerated containers. Historical Tuesday brining window: breasts about 8 AM–6 PM; whole bird about 8 AM–8 PM.
  2. Remove from brine and dry thoroughly. Refrigerate uncovered on racks; avoid automatically adding more salt after commercial wet brining.
  3. Thursday morning: place seasoned butter under the skin (confirmed). Exterior butter and rub application were probable in 2025; use a thin neutral-oil coating and lighter rub for 2026. Inject meat with cooled injection.
  4. Historical Traeger plan: 7 AM at 225°F; 9 AM to 275°F; add breasts around 10 AM; finish at 325–350°F around noon only if skin color allows. These are planning checkpoints, not guaranteed cook times.
  5. Use independent probe readings in the thickest breast and thigh; poultry must reach 165°F. Rest and carve in time for 1:30 PM service.

2025: flavor and moisture were good; skin too dark. 2026 experiment: lighter exterior rub, avoid sugar/honey on skin, dry uncovered, monitor color. Exact rub amounts and actual smoker temperatures not confirmed.

Turkey injection — final 1.5× version

Ingredients & instructions
  • 3 cups cooled homemade turkey stock
  • 3/4 cup unsalted melted butter
  • 3 tbsp poultry seasoning
  • 1 1/2 tbsp garlic powder
  • 1 1/2 tbsp onion powder
  • 1 tbsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tbsp salt
  • 1 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • Optional: 1–3 tsp sugar
  • Optional: pinch cayenne
  1. Warm stock and butter just enough to combine.
  2. Whisk in seasoning; strain very well to prevent injector clogs.
  3. Chill promptly and keep refrigerated; warm only enough to flow through injector just before use.
  4. Inject breasts generously, then thighs, drumsticks and thick wings; stop when liquid pushes back.
  5. Do not brush any injection that has contacted raw poultry onto cooked food.

This final ingredient list supersedes an earlier itinerary that mentioned Worcestershire, maple/honey and rubs. Salt load should be reviewed alongside commercial brine.

Compound butter

Ingredients & instructions
  • 4 sticks unsalted butter
  • Poultry seasoning, to taste
  • Meat Church Hickory and Hail Mary rubs, to taste (probable 2025 combination)
  1. Soften butter enough to mix; the original shorthand said melt, mix, refrigerate.
  2. Mix in seasonings and refrigerate until needed.
  3. Work under loosened turkey skin Thursday morning; exterior use in 2025 is probable, not confirmed.

No exact seasoning measurements were recorded. Keep this recipe intentionally adjustable.

Roasted Thanksgiving broth

Ingredients & instructions
  • 6–8 lb turkey wings/necks or chicken wings/necks
  • Olive oil, kosher salt, pepper
  • 1 smoked ham hock or smoked turkey part
  • 5–6 qt water, plus more as needed
  • 2 celery stalks
  • 1 large yellow onion
  • 1 parsnip
  • 1 fennel bulb
  • 1 head garlic
  • 4 bay leaves
  • 3 dried shiitake mushrooms
  • 2 dried guajillo chiles
  • 1 tbsp black peppercorns
  • 1/2 bunch parsley
  • 1/2 bunch thyme
  1. Roast poultry parts at 425°F until deeply golden, roughly 90 minutes for turkey parts or 45 minutes for chicken; turn halfway.
  2. Reserve rendered fat for gravy. Deglaze roasting tray with 1/2 cup water and add browned bits to stockpot.
  3. Add roasted bones, smoked hock and enough water to cover; simmer very gently 2–3 hours.
  4. Add remaining vegetables, aromatics and herbs; simmer another 2 hours.
  5. Strain and chill promptly. Refrigerate for 2–3 days or freeze longer.

Plan sufficient total broth for gravy, injection, stuffing and reheating; four-quart yield is approximate.

Make-ahead turkey gravy

Ingredients & instructions
  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 2 shallots
  • 3 garlic cloves
  • 1/3 cup dry sherry or Marsala wine (about 79 mL)
  • 4 tbsp butter
  • 4 tbsp reserved poultry fat
  • 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
  • 4 cups Thanksgiving broth
  • 4 thyme sprigs
  • 2 rosemary sprigs
  • 4 sage leaves
  • 2–3 tsp soy sauce
  • 1–2 tsp Worcestershire
  • Salt and black pepper
  • Optional 1 tsp red wine vinegar
  1. Sauté shallots in oil about 5 minutes; add garlic and cook 2 more minutes.
  2. Deglaze with sherry or Marsala and reduce nearly dry.
  3. Melt in butter and reserved fat; stir in flour and cook 1–2 minutes.
  4. Whisk in broth gradually and bring to a simmer; add herbs and simmer 20–30 minutes, stirring.
  5. Add soy sauce and Worcestershire; season, add vinegar if desired, strain and cool.
  6. Reheat gently, whisking and thinning with stock if needed. If frozen, thaw overnight in refrigerator or reheat gently from frozen, stirring constantly. Bring to a full boil and whisk in clean cooked turkey drippings if available.

Photo shows two containers labeled Turkey Gravy 11/5. Packet gravy was also staged as a backup in the 2025 itinerary.

Mom’s turkey stuffing — doubled family batch

Ingredients & instructions
  • 4 onions
  • 12 garlic cloves
  • 1/2 lb butter = 2 standard sticks
  • 2 lb pork sausage
  • 12 eggs
  • 2 small Italian loaves or roughly 2 lb unseasoned bread cubes
  • About 2 tbsp parsley
  • Black pepper, to taste
  • Allspice, to taste
  • Cumin seed, to taste
  • Other spices as desired
  • 1 full packet Lipton onion soup mix
  1. Dry bread cubes at 225°F, per note on original card.
  2. Sauté onions and garlic in 1/2 lb butter for the doubled batch until medium brown.
  3. Add sausage; cook about 15 minutes until thoroughly cooked. Cool before mixing in eggs.
  4. Combine with eggs, diced bread, parsley, spices and full packet onion soup mix.
  5. Bake as dressing in a casserole until center reaches 165°F. The original card also allowed stuffing a turkey, but baking separately is the planned safer approach.

Original single batch: 2 onions; 6 garlic cloves; 1/4 lb butter; 1 lb sausage; 6 eggs; 1 small Italian loaf; 1 tbsp parsley; 1/2 packet Lipton. Original photograph preserved unchanged.

Mozzarella & pepperoni stuffing

Ingredients & instructions
  • 3 tbsp unsalted butter, plus butter for bread
  • 3 medium onions
  • 8 celery stalks
  • 12 slices white sandwich bread
  • Salt and white pepper
  • 2 tbsp fresh thyme
  • 10 fresh sage leaves
  • 1 tsp dried rosemary
  • 10 oz pepperoni
  • 1 lb bulk breakfast sausage
  • 1 lb firm mozzarella
  • 1 cup heated low-sodium chicken stock
  1. Heat oven to 375°F. Sauté onions and celery in 2 tbsp butter until translucent.
  2. Toast bread slices until lightly brown, butter both sides and cube; toss with salt, pepper and herbs.
  3. Brown diced pepperoni in remaining butter for 2–3 minutes; drain. Brown sausage about 10 minutes.
  4. Combine bread, vegetables, meats and cubed mozzarella. Add heated stock to moisten.
  5. Transfer to buttered 3-qt baking dish. Bake covered about 30 minutes, then uncovered roughly 20 minutes, until center reaches 165°F.

Both stuffing recipes were served in 2025 and quantities were sufficient. 2026 schedule must account for this recipe’s 375°F preference versus the shared 350°F oven block.

Fresh buttermilk mashed potatoes

Ingredients & instructions
  • 5 lb Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes
  • 2 1/2 cups heavy cream
  • 5 sticks unsalted butter
  • 1/2–3/4 cup buttermilk
  • Salt, to taste
  • Optional pepper, chives, roasted garlic
  1. Wednesday: peel and cut 5 lb potatoes into even 2-inch chunks. Cover completely with cold water, cover container and refrigerate at 40°F or below for no more than 24 hours. Measure dairy separately and refrigerate.
  2. Thursday 10:45 AM: drain and cover with fresh cold salted water. Bring to boil, then simmer until completely tender, about 20–30 minutes after boiling; allow extra time at altitude.
  3. Drain well; return to warm pot briefly to release steam. Rice or mash while hot.
  4. Fold in warm butter first, then gradually add warm cream. Add buttermilk last to taste; season and avoid overmixing.
  5. Around noon transfer to preheated slow cooker on WARM if it holds at least 140°F. Stir and adjust consistency at 1:15 PM; serve at 1:30 PM.

Historical alternative: bake whole scored potatoes at 425°F for 55–75 minutes, peel, rice hot, then butter, cream and buttermilk in that order. 2025 likely used boiled potatoes cooked Wednesday; 2026 uses fresh Thursday cooking.

Family candied sweet potatoes — triple batch

Ingredients & instructions
  • 6 lb sweet potatoes
  • 3 cups packed brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp salt
  • 3/4 cup butter (1 1/2 sticks)
  • 1 1/2 cups water
  1. Parboil whole sweet potatoes about 15 minutes; cool enough to peel and cut into rounds or chunks.
  2. Melt butter in baking dish. Bring water, brown sugar, salt and butter to a boil; simmer about 3 minutes.
  3. Pour syrup over potatoes in two dishes if needed. Bake at 350°F for 60–75 minutes, basting often.
  4. Prepare fully Wednesday; refrigerate and reheat Thursday until hot.

Original note also says “Bake for 400 degrees for 20–25 minutes” before parboiling directions; conflicting instruction retained as unresolved, not added to the main method. Actual 2025 platter shows cubed sweet potatoes.

Green bean casserole — doubled

Ingredients & instructions
  • 6 slices thick-cut bacon
  • 1 cup diced yellow onion
  • 4 garlic cloves
  • 24 oz fresh mushrooms
  • 6 tbsp butter
  • 6 tbsp flour
  • 2 cups half-and-half
  • 2 cups chicken broth
  • 1 cup shredded white cheddar
  • 1 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 2 lb fresh green beans
  • 2 cans French fried onions
  1. Trim and halve beans; blanch 5 minutes, ice bath 2 minutes, drain well.
  2. Cook bacon until crisp; sauté onion 4–5 minutes, then garlic and mushrooms another 4–5 minutes. Set aside.
  3. Melt butter, whisk in flour and cook 2 minutes; slowly whisk in half-and-half and broth.
  4. Melt in cheddar; add bacon, mushrooms, salt and pepper; simmer 2 minutes, fold in beans.
  5. Assemble in 9×13 dish Wednesday without fried onions; refrigerate.
  6. Thursday top with onions and bake uncovered at 350°F about 30 minutes; allow longer from refrigerator and verify hot center.

2025 doubled amount was sufficient. For better topping texture, add fried onions late if they darken too quickly.

Family cranberry-cherry Jell-O salad

Ingredients & instructions
  • 2 small packages cherry Jell-O
  • 1 cup hot water
  • 3/4 cup sugar
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 cup pineapple juice
  • 1 package ground cranberries (weight unrecorded)
  • 1 orange, ground
  • 1 cup crushed pineapple, drained
  • 1 cup chopped celery
  • 1/2 cup chopped pecans
  1. Dissolve Jell-O completely in hot water.
  2. Add sugar, lemon juice and pineapple juice.
  3. Chill until mixture begins to set.
  4. Mix cranberries, orange, pineapple, celery and pecans; fold into partially set Jell-O.
  5. Refrigerate until firm.

Original screenshot preserved. Confirm cranberry package weight and gelatin package size before grocery purchase.

Leftover turkey tetrazzini

Ingredients & instructions
  • 1/2 lb spaghetti
  • 2–3 tbsp butter
  • 1 garlic clove
  • 2 tbsp flour
  • 1 1/4 cups chicken broth
  • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • About 1 lb cooked turkey
  • 1 cup cooked green beans or casserole
  • 1 cup corn
  • Optional 1/2 cup peas
  • 1/2 cup shredded cheddar
  • 1/4 cup Parmesan
  • 1/2 cup panko
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • Salt and pepper
  1. Cook pasta al dente.
  2. Sauté garlic in 2 tbsp butter; whisk in flour 1 minute, then broth and cream; simmer until thick.
  3. Stir in turkey, green beans, corn, optional peas and cheddar; combine with pasta.
  4. Transfer to greased 8×8 dish. Top with panko, Parmesan and olive oil.
  5. Bake 350°F for 20–25 minutes; rest 10 minutes.

Not part of Thanksgiving Day menu. No mushrooms in this adaptation.

Turkey Command Center

What we know from 2025

20–22 lb spatchcocked turkey and 9–11 lb additional breasts planned for 2026. In 2025, two Meat Church brine packages were used. Hickory and Hail Mary rubs are probable; seasoned butter under skin is confirmed; exterior butter is probable.

The turkey tasted good. Skin was too dark in places.

2026 controlled improvements

Keep commercial brine and under-skin butter. Do not automatically add a second salt-heavy dry brine. Dry uncovered in the fridge, use lighter exterior rub, avoid sugar/honey on the surface and watch skin color closely during finishing heat.

Safety: poultry and stuffing should reach 165°F; confirm with a reliable thermometer. Use the timeline as an estimate, not a guarantee.
